text:
nina: Quick flag from the magnet-7b-int4 onboarding runs: we see reproducible small-context drift after ~9k tokens when using our new packed-KV layout for int4. Not as noisy as previous int8 case but subtle punctuation and identifier swaps in code outputs.

nina: Setup: model=magnet-7b:int4pack, prime 9k (docs+code), gen 500, with kv-checkpoint enabled every 1500 tokens. Ran 3 seeds. All three seeds show divergence at ~9100-9200.

raj: do we see any layer-local corruption or is it distributed?

nina: initial inspect: layer 23/27 shows small offset in KV value shard offsets (byte offset mod 16 != 0) only on pack-mode. fp16 and software-unpacked int4 are aligned.

	logs:
```
[INFO] kvcache: layer=23 shard=2 write_offset=16384 expected_align=16368
[WARN] packer: tail_pad=6 bytes (unfilled)
[ERROR] memcpy: copy_size=2040 expected=2048
```


tom: tail_pad=6 is suspicious. our vector kernel wants 8- or 16-byte alignment. Could be compute->gpu packing rounding.

nina: hypothesis: our int4 pack routine (v2) changed the tile stride calc to optimize memory, but misses padding when tile_size % pack_gran != 0. That leaves garbage in the last partial byte which persists into snapshots.

raj: consequence being small fp differences -> attention rescale slightly -> RoPE phase energy changes on long-distance tokens -> drift cascades. Makes sense.

nina: repro command I used:
```
python -m experiments.longctx_onboard \
  --model magnet-7b:int4pack \
  --prime tests/9k_long_mixed.txt \
  --prime-len 9000 \
  --gen-len 500 \
  --kv-checkpoint true \
  --ckpt-interval 1500 \
  --seed 7 \
  --save-snap /tmp/mag7b_int4pack_seed7/
```


dave: can you run with --force-align=16 and also with --pack-fallback-software to see if this goes away?

nina: started those two runs on canary-02. ETA ~12m. Also kicking off a cross-compare that replays first 5 snapshots from fp16, int4pack, and int4-sof and compares per-layer max-abs diffs for K and V. Output will be CSV.

ci-bot: ci job 2026.03.21.18 queued for branch "pack-fix-probe"; artifacts at s3://redwood-ci/pack-fix-probe/20260321-1812 if needed.

raj: small note: our eval harness (longcode-eval) is very sensitive to punctuation in multi-line code. even a dropped colon will fail exact-match tests. So these small diffs are high-impact.

nina: early results: with --force-align=16 the pack path passes through without tail_pad warnings and the generation matches fp16 up to 12k tokens (ran extended test). With software fallback pack the outputs match fp16 exactly for the whole 10k run. So pack packing appears to be the cause.

	compare summary snippet:
```
layer,mode,snapshot,max_abs(K),max_abs(V)
23,fp16,5,0.0,0.0
23,int4pack,5,1.2e-03,8.9e-04
23,int4soft,5,0.0,0.0
```

raj: perfect repro and a solid guardrail. Next we should: 1) add an assert in packer that tail_pad==0 or we force-zero last byte before writing snapshots, and 2) add a nightly longctx roundtrip test with int4pack to catch regressions.

nina: created PR draft with soft-guard (zero-fill last byte + metric kvcache.pack_truncated_count). Will also add telemetry so we can query how often this happens in production.

	PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021 (draft)

short diff excerpt:
```
- // pack tiles into contiguous buffer
- pack_tail(...)
+ // ensure last partial byte is zeroed to avoid snapshot nondet
+ if (tail_pad) memset(tail_ptr, 0, tail_pad);
+ pack_tail(...)
```

ci-bot: lint and unit tests passed for PR 4021 on branch pack-fix-probe.

tom: after PR merges let's run a canary burn (48h) with magnet-7b:int4pack on a couple of high-usage shards to confirm telemetry. Also add the pack-alignment flag to the runtime CLI so teams can toggle until fully validated.

nina: agreed. I'll merge after one more review and schedule canary. Also attaching a minimal diff example showing the symptom in generated code:
```
fp16: "def compute(x):\n    if x > 0:\n        return x * 2\n"
int4pack (prefix issue): "def compute(x):\n    if x > 0\n        return x * 2\n"
```
(note missing colon)

raj: thanks for catching this. Good catch on the packer change. Great triage.

nina: tagging @eng-ml for visibility. I'll keep uploads and final metrics in s3://redwood-debug/pack-truncation/1748629999/ and update this thread when canary finishes. :white_check_mark:
